title: Lawanda N NDE 4814
content: The first time I was too young to remember as I was only three weeks old. However, I was told that my grandfather was a medicine man from the Aniyawanyah people (Cherokee), and he came to the hospital to see me after the accident. The attending nurse said he put his hands over my body and said something in his native tongue, and left. About two hours later, she was downstairs at the hospital filing some documents and heard a baby crying. She walked into the morgue where I was lying on a gurney, and found me breathing and shivering and crying. She took me up, wrapped me in a blanket, and immediately had me put in critical care for infants and in an incubator. As I grew up, I was treated differently because I seemed to have the ability to predict things before they happened. I was a bit isolated by family because of this. They thought something was wrong with me and even accused me of being possessed because they were heavily religious with the Methodist faith and were astonished at the things I foreseen that came true. The second event I was thrown from a horse. I can remember being dragged through a barbed wire fence and then thrown to the ground where a sharp tree stump went through my left eye. I can remember watching my adopted mother picking my limp body up and screaming for my adopted father to get some towels. I was not feeling pain and could not understand why they could not hear me telling them I was okay. I remember things getting bright several times, then getting dark and feeling intense pressure on my breathing. It was like darting from one scenario to another, one minute I was in this long brightly lit place, like a hallway with no floor or ceiling or windows or doors. Then another minute, I was in severe pain and could not see but could hear the panic in everyone. I remember screaming for my dad not to leave me but I could see, and I could see my dead aunty telling me it was okay and not to be afraid - after this I was afraid of water because I was on a ship in a stormy sea and it was dark and lightening all around and people were fighting. However to this day I have never been on a ship or on the ocean and I refuse to go on any ship or boat where I cannot see land nearby. The third event was when I went into early labor with my daughter. I remember her being born. I remember watching it happen, and as she was born, my partner was rushed out of the delivery room, and I followed him in to the lobby. When I got out there his mother and sister and father had arrived. I could see them as if I was looking down on them. I even watched my partner faint. I remember laughing at him because I thought he fainted from watching our daughter being born. Later I found out it was because he was told I had died. To this day, they say there is no way I could have known that because I never left the delivery room and that my heart had stopped three times during the birth. When the doctors got me stabilized, they began to allow my daughter to breast feed. I was rushed to critical care for days. During this time, I believe I was in a semi-coma for a while because I kept going back and forth to reality then to a place where my deceased fiancé was. I carried on a conversation with him about why I could not go with him. He convinced me to go back to my kids and present partner because they needed me. When I came out of the coma state, it was like I was falling and gasping for breath. I reached up and grabbed the bedrails to stop my fall. Then I could not breathe very easily. I could hear the nurses and my partner scurrying around in a panic-like state and concerned voices saying 'She is waking up, the hard parts over now,' but I could not seem to find the strength to open my eyes or move again. After that, my body felt like it had a large flat stone lying on top of me.

tunnel.passage_other_detail: A long brightly lit place like a hallway with no floor or ceiling or windows or doors; also described darkness with intense pressure on breathing and darting between scenarios.
tunnel.movement_other_detail: Described 'darting from one scenario to another' and later 'falling' on return.

arrival.other_being_detail: Deceased aunty; deceased fiancé (during semi-coma period after childbirth).

environment.environment_other_detail: Bright hallway-like space without typical physical features; also a stormy sea/ship scene with lightning and fighting.

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: Described coming out of coma 'like I was falling and gasping for breath' and grabbing bedrails to stop the fall.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Three events: (1) infant accident with presumed death and placement in morgue; (2) thrown from a horse with traumatic eye injury; (3) childbirth/early labor with heart stopping three times and semi-coma.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Stormy sea/ship scene with lightning and fighting; repeated bright-to-dark transitions; semi-coma oscillation between realities.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Described darting between scenes (bright hallway, pain/darkness with panic sounds, deceased aunty present, ship in storm) rather than a single linear progression; later (childbirth) OBE to lobby and repeated returns during semi-coma.
stage_sequence.repeated_stage_detail: Repeated transitions between bright and dark scenes; 'kept going back and forth to reality then to a place where my deceased fiancé was.'

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Reported a stormy ship/sea scene and long-term phobia of water/boats despite never having been on the ocean; infant incident involved being found alive in the morgue after presumed death; family attributed later precognition to possession.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “It was like darting from one scenario to another, one minute I was in this long brightly lit place, like a hallway with no floor or ceiling or windows or doors.”; “When I came out of the coma state, it was like I was falling and gasping for breath.”; “She is waking up, the hard parts over now.”
